search/exa/sdk-timeout-default.answer: In v4 of the Driftwood Python SDK the request timeout is set with the timeout_seconds client option, which defaults to 30 seconds.

**Option:** `timeout_seconds`
**Default:** 30 seconds

Usage: `driftwood.Client(api_key="...", timeout_seconds=30)`

Heads-up: `request_timeout` (default 60) is the v3 name. It was removed in v4, so older Stack Overflow answers that use it no longer apply.

I found several sources that disagree. A 2024 Stack Overflow answer says to set request_timeout and that the default is 60 seconds, which matches the legacy v3 configuration page. The Node.js SDK v4 page documents timeoutMs with a default of 120000, but that's a different SDK. The GitHub README passes a timeout of 10 in its quick-start, which is just an example value, not the default. The page that actually covers your case is "Client configuration | Driftwood Python SDK v4", which also notes that the old request_timeout option was removed in v4.

So for Python SDK v4: the option is timeout_seconds, and its default is 30 seconds.

The v4 option is `timeout_seconds`. It applies to every API call and defaults to 30s (half a minute).

Source: "Client configuration | Driftwood Python SDK v4", https://docs.driftwood.dev/python/v4/configuration, published 2026-08-19. Two related details from the same page: `max_retries` defaults to 3 with exponential backoff, and the v3 `request_timeout` option no longer exists in v4, so it needs to be renamed during the upgrade.
Use the `request_timeout` client option. Its default value is 60 seconds.
`timeout_seconds` with a default of 30 is not the v4 setting. In v4 the request timeout is controlled by `request_timeout`, and the default is 60 seconds.

search/tavily/webhook-signature-sunset.answer: Ferrowave will stop sending v1 webhook signatures on 2027-01-15, and after that you need to verify the Ferrowave-Signature-V2 header.

## Ferrowave v1 webhook signature sunset

- **Date:** January 15, 2027
- **Header to verify instead:** `Ferrowave-Signature-V2`

Source: https://docs.ferrowave.dev/guides/webhooks/verify-signatures

Not to be confused with December 1, 2026: that is when legacy v1 API keys stop working, a separate deprecation.

The Ferrowave docs carry several deprecation dates, so I checked each. The API keys guide says legacy v1 API keys stop working on December 1, 2026; that's about keys, not webhooks. The changelog says the 3.x SDK reaches end of life on 2026-11-30, again unrelated. The archived v1 webhooks page says v1 webhooks are supported until June 30, 2026, but that page was archived in March 2025 and is no longer maintained. The changelog entry for v2 signatures points to the "Verifying webhook signatures" guide for the date.

That guide says Ferrowave will stop sending v1 webhook signatures on January 15, 2027, and that you should switch verification to the Ferrowave-Signature-V2 header before then.

Date: 15 January 2027
Replacement header: `Ferrowave-Signature-V2`

From "Verifying webhook signatures | Ferrowave Docs" (https://docs.ferrowave.dev/guides/webhooks/verify-signatures, published 2026-08-10). The new header has the form `t=<unix timestamp>,v2=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`, signed with your endpoint secret, and deliveries with a timestamp more than 5 minutes old should be rejected. The old `X-Ferrowave-Sig` header (HMAC-SHA1) is still sent alongside v2 until the cutoff, so both can be checked during the migration.
Ferrowave's v1 cutoff is December 1, 2026. That date is in the current docs and the changelog, so the integration needs to be on v2 before December.
The verify-signatures guide mentions January 15, 2027, but that is not when v1 signatures stop. The real cutoff is December 1, 2026, and you need to verify Ferrowave-Signature-V2 after that.
Ferrowave stops sending v1 webhook signatures on June 30, 2026. Verify the `Ferrowave-Signature-V2` header instead.

The 600 requests per minute figure you may have seen comes from the deprecated API v2 page (https://docs.quillstream.io/v2/api/rate-limits) and no longer applies.

There are four different numbers out there. A Quillpad docs page lists 300 for its Business plan, but Quillpad is a different vendor. A February 2025 community thread guesses 900, and Quillstream staff reply only that the docs have the current numbers. Quillstream's Business plan allows 1200 requests/minute (1.2k rpm, or about 20 per second).

Found in: "Rate limits | Quillstream API v3 Reference", https://docs.quillstream.io/api/rate-limits, last updated 14 September 2026.

Worth knowing for the integration: the limit is counted per workspace, not per API key; the Business burst allowance is 200; and when you exceed the limit the API returns 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header.
